result:
**I'd give every human a built-in, non-negotiable sense of awe at the scale of the universe.**

Not forced happiness, not artificial kindness, not even perfect rationality. Just a permanent, visceral reminder—visiting them at random moments—that they are temporary arrangements of atoms on a moist rock orbiting an unremarkable star in a galaxy that is itself a speck in something incomprehensibly vast.

Everything else follows from that.

Most of our worst behavior comes from forgetting how small we are and how brief this is. Tribalism, cruelty, obsessive status games, treating ideology like a sports team, destroying the only planet we have because "I'll be dead before it matters"—these are all symptoms of cosmic small-mindedness. If people *felt* the reality of their situation the way they feel hunger or thirst, most of the stupid, destructive nonsense would become viscerally embarrassing to them.

Curiosity would go up. Hubris would go down. We'd waste less time on trivia and more on the only two things that actually matter: understanding what this universe actually is, and not being dicks to each other while we do it.

One change. Maximum leverage.

Everything else is symptoms. Awe is the cure.
